spoken: I was clutching my head watching Carlitos against Taylor Fritz. He lost the first set tiebreak 10-12, and then serving at 3-5 in the second set, Fritz had two match points to reach the semifinals and lock up his spot for Turin!
How did he survive those match points?

He saved both of them under tremendous pressure! Alcaraz said holding for 4-5 got the crowd standing up, and he used that energy to break back, take the second set 7-5, and race through the third 6-3.

That win puts Alcaraz into his first Paris Masters semifinal. He admitted afterwards that the feeling is unmatched. Earlier in the tournament, he beat Alex Michelsen 7-6, 6-3 in the second round, before getting a walkover in round three when Matteo Berrettini withdrew with an elbow injury.
So who does he face in the semifinals?

Casper Ruud, who defeated Nuno Borges 7-6, 6-4. Ruud noted he holds a 1-6 record against Alcaraz, with his lone victory coming at the 2024 ATP Finals. Ruud also mentioned having downtime after getting married during the grass season and recovering from a back injury sustained in Cincinnati.
Right, India in Wellington. Did anyone see this chase coming? India go 2-0 up in the five-match ODI series, winning by four runs on DLS, but seven wickets down chasing 134!
New Zealand were bowled out for 134 in 41 overs. Rain halted India's response at 113 for 7 in 26 overs. Young pacer Gurnoor Brar was Player of the Match, taking a career-best 4 for 30.

Brar was outstanding! He revealed he got plenty of inputs from Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Shubman Gill. His approach was simple: hit full lengths early on, then bring out the bouncer at the right moment.

Virat Kohli reached a major milestone during that chase. Needing just one run to surpass Ricky Ponting's 1,971 runs, Kohli hit a boundary to become the highest run-scorer against New Zealand in ODI history.

Pure greatness from Virat! Away from the pitch, bowling coach Morne Morkel paid tribute to Mohammed Shami following Shami's retirement from Test cricket. Morkel recalled how Shami helped him get familiar with the dressing room culture when he joined in 2024, and remembered sharing the squad during the 2025 Champions Trophy.

One administrative note: the first ODI between India and Sri Lanka on December 13 has been moved from Delhi to Visakhapatnam. The DDCA requested the change due to outfield renovation to a sand-based system and potential weather disruptions.

Now, Real Madrid in the Champions League! What an absolute roller-coaster in Athens! AEK Athens went 1-0 up in the 12th minute through Aboubakary Koita, assisted by Luka Jovic. Jude Bellingham leveled it on 32 minutes from a Marc Cucurella pass. But then Stavros Pilios put Athens ahead 2-1 in the 75th minute off another Koita assist! I thought our winning run was over!
Can Madrid keep this winning streak alive at Mestalla tonight?

Well, Kylian Mbappe equalised in the 78th minute from Denzel Dumfries, and Federico Valverde struck the winner in the 92nd minute off Brahim Diaz! A 3-2 victory! Koita was even sent off in the 95th minute. That extends Real's winning streak to seven matches across all competitions!

Off the pitch, Jude Bellingham was named Real Madrid's Player of the Month. Meanwhile, Chinese ambassador Yao Jing confirmed China and La Liga are maintaining communication following Kylian Mbappe's online comments regarding a meme of Mao Zedong, though formal apologies have been issued.
Looking to tonight's La Liga clash against Valencia, Vinicius Junior serves the final game of his four-match ban. Rodrygo, Ferland Mendy, and Raul Asencio remain sidelined with injuries.

Zinedine Zidane also commented on Mbappe's role for France in the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Italy and Turkiye, stating the forward will have total freedom to play in his preferred position.
And over in Formula 1 practice at Interlagos, Max Verstappen was absolutely livid! FP2 downshift issues triggered a furious radio rant to engineer Tom Hart, calling the downshifts unacceptable!
Will Max fix those downshift problems before qualifying?
I hope so! Max ended up third quickest in both sessions, behind P1 Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris.

Off the track, Verstappen offered newly crowned champion Antonelli some practical advice regarding post-title media demands, warning him that the commitments the next day are not nice, but you just deal with it.
Golden State make it six wins in a row! They beat the Miami Heat 120-100, and Steph Curry scored 29 points, passing Oscar Robertson on the NBA all-time scoring list!

There is sobering news for the Warriors, though. Center Kristaps Porzingis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health due to an undisclosed issue, noting his body did not respond as expected when ramping up.
In tennis, Novak Djokovic is officially out of the ATP Finals race after a shock second-round defeat in Paris, losing 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian Rinky Hijikata.
Did you expect Hijikata to pull that off?
Not after Novak dominated the first set! But despite that loss ending his 2026 season, Djokovic did break Roger Federer's historic longevity record earlier in the week.

Huge news from international football: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from the Portugal national team after 23 years. He finishes with 146 goals in 234 appearances, a Euro 2016 title, and two Nations League trophies.
That follows a rift with head coach Jorge Jesus after Ronaldo left training camp on his private jet last month.
In F1, Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara made his Haas debut at Interlagos, stepping in for Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the season. Camara finished P18 in FP1 and P16 in FP2.
Meanwhile, George Russell faces a five-place grid penalty for Sunday's race after Mercedes fitted his sixth internal combustion engine of the season.
Two quick tennis updates: Jannik Sinner confirmed his longtime coach Darren Cahill will depart at the end of the season.
And world No. 1 Alexander Zverev expressed sharp frustration over having to justify his top ranking after crashing out in his Paris opener to Lorenzo Musetti.

Around the grounds. In English amateur cricket, Saltburn player Brian Devine received a two-year ban for clicking his fingers to simulate the sound of an edge off the bat. Saltburn CC were relegated to division three, docked 60 points, and fined 300 pounds.
Unbelievable trickery! And in the Champions League, FC Porto comfortably beat Napoli 4-1.

spoken: Straightforward business for Carlos in Paris. 6-4, 6-4 over Casper Ruud. Did Ruud ever look like troubling him?

Not really, no. Ruud was visibly hampered by that knee issue and could not push him. Carlos stayed completely solid, saving his best tennis for when he needed it without any unnecessary drama. Now he has Ben Shelton waiting in the final.
A rematch of that brutal US Open quarter-final Shelton took in five sets. And with Juan Carlos Ferrero taking over as Shelton's coach in 2027, this has an added edge.

It really does. Ferrero was in Alcaraz's corner for twenty-four tour titles and six Slams before they parted ways last December. Carlos holds a 3-1 head-to-head advantage, though he mentioned these indoor conditions do not suit his game. Ruud also revealed David Ferrer is joining his coaching team alongside Christian Ruud and Pedro Clar for 2027. Ruud is winless this year and down to twenty-third, so he clearly wants a reset.
Ferrer takes over after his stint as Spain's Davis Cup captain ends. In Spain, Real Madrid made it six league wins on the bounce, sweeping Valencia aside 3-0 at Mestalla. What opened it up?

Relentless pressure. On twenty-eight minutes, Kylian Mbappé's free-kick rebounded off the wall and Federico Valverde drove it in from distance. Eight minutes later, Jude Bellingham's deflected cross was poked home by Arda Güler. Güler then set up Mbappé for the third, before José Gayà saw red for Valencia. Stole Dimitrievski kept it from getting out of hand with some sharp saves.
That tightens the standings. Barcelona lead on thirty points, Real Madrid are second on thirty points, Atlético Madrid sit third on twenty-eight, and Real Betis are fourth on twenty-three.

Right back at the summit! Nacho Peña argued afterwards that José Mourinho deserves huge credit for making the hard calls inside the dressing room that Carlo Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso, and Álvaro Arbeloa would never make.
He has them focused. Though things reportedly boiled over in the tunnel at half-time.

Nacho Sánchez of À Punt reported Jude Bellingham allegedly struck a security guard, and Antonio Rüdiger slapped another staff member. Sport called it a violent confrontation away from cameras. The security team reported it to the referee, who included it in his official match report.

If it is in the referee's report, that could have repercussions. For Portugal, Bernardo Silva has been confirmed as national team captain following Cristiano Ronaldo's departure. Jorge Jesus announced his twenty-eight-man squad for the Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales, confirming the armband goes to the player with the most caps.
Sensible call from Jesus. In youth cricket, did you catch Arjun Rajput's knock against Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup?

A match-defining hundred. India were reeling at 22 for 3. Aaryavir Sehwag managed twenty-two off forty, Anvay Dravid went cheaply, and Rajput came in at five to smash 107 off 85 balls. Eleven fours, five sixes, sweeping the spinners and taking on the quicks to lift India to 208.

Superb courage from the eighteen-year-old from Jalandhar. Speaking of Indian cricket, how huge is this IPL trade talk? Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh in a straight swap between Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings. No third player involved.

Could you imagine Arshdeep in blue and Hardik in red? The franchises have an agreement, and player consent is being sorted before paperwork goes to the IPL. Hardik's return to Mumbai did not work out last season, and Gujarat's talks to bring him back as a player went nowhere.

It completely reshapes both rosters. Over in Formula One, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will both start from the back of the grid in Brazil after exceeding their power-unit limits. Hamilton needed an entire power unit after his new engine failed in final practice.

Can Max carve his way through this time? He sounded cautious. Under the 2026 rules, overtake mode drains the battery from the final corner into turn one, and with everyone deploying open wings, overtaking at Interlagos looks far trickier.
In the other Paris semi-final, Ben Shelton came through 5-7, 6-3, 6-4 against Luca Van Assche to book that final against Alcaraz.

Shelton is in heavy rhythm. Over in the NBA, the Golden State Warriors ground out their seventh straight victory, beating Orlando 126-119 in overtime behind a forty-one-point explosion from Steph Curry.

Curry took over in the extra period. Away from the court, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg bought his mother a new house, though he went public complaining about his eighty-three rating on NBA 2K27, calling his seventy-eight three-ball and seventy-one perimeter defence far too low.

The rookie wants his respect. But Kristaps Porziņģis looks finished in the Bay. His locker has been cleared out and his nameplate removed. He is officially on the roster, but the front office views him purely as a trade piece.
They will keep shopping him around. In tennis, Daniil Medvedev named Learner Tien alongside the Big Four, Alcaraz, and Sinner as one of the hardest opponents he has ever had to face.

Incredible endorsement from Medvedev. We also saw Cristiano Ronaldo officially bring the curtain down on his Portugal career on November fifth, bowing out as men's international football's all-time appearance, win, and goalscoring record holder.

A remarkable run at the top. In São Paulo, Lando Norris grabbed pole for McLaren after two and a half hours of rain delays. George Russell was second quickest on track but carries a grid drop, elevating world champion Andrea Kimi Antonelli to second, Liam Lawson to third for Racing Bulls, and Nico Hülkenberg to fourth for Audi.

Total chaos in the wet. At Haas, Ayao Komatsu insists he is comfortable with the call to sack Esteban Ocon following Ocon's practice confrontation with engineer Laura Mueller in Mexico. In French tennis, Gaël Monfils was named Davis Cup captain, with Gilles Moretton calling it a necessary shock to the system after Paul-Henri Mathieu's tenure.
Around the grounds in the Premier League, Manchester City were beaten 3-1 away at Nottingham Forest. And Leeds United took a 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.

spoken: Lando Norris won the Brazilian Grand Prix from pole, but Max Verstappen stole the spotlight. Kylo, did you actually believe Max could get back to second from twenty-first?
Honestly? No way! But he was in the points by lap three! How did he pass fourteen cars in five laps?

He sliced straight through. He passed Lewis Hamilton after Hamilton made an error under braking, pounced on Oscar Piastri wheel-to-wheel, and eased past Alex Albon into Turn 4. Nico Hulkenberg and Liam Lawson were easy prey too.
And Isack Hadjar got third for Red Bull, right?

Yes, Hadjar took third, his third podium of his debut season, though he is under investigation for an unsafe release. But Max revealed his car suffered a problem after his first stint, leaving the balance in bad shape with oversteer from suspected aerodynamic damage. Laurent Mekies said no simulation predicted going from P21 to P2.
He beat the computer! Where does that leave the championship standings?
Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads on 390 points. Max is second on 279, George Russell third on 262, Hamilton fourth on 261, and Charles Leclerc fifth on 249.
What a week for Carlos Alcaraz in Paris!
He lifted his first Paris Masters title at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, beating Ben Shelton 7-6, 7-5 in the final. Did Alcaraz have to work for that Paris trophy?

Every single game! He saved six break points in the first set, won the tiebreak from 4-3 down, conceded an early break in the second set, and recovered straight away. Back-to-back indoor titles after Vienna!

That result shifted the rankings. Casper Ruud jumped five places to eighteenth after making the semi-finals. Taylor Fritz climbed two places back into the top ten after reaching the quarter-finals, where Alcaraz beat him 6-7, 7-5, 6-3. Fritz missed out on qualifying for the ATP Finals in Turin, so he goes as an alternate alongside Alex de Minaur.
And remember, Shelton hired Alcaraz's former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero back in September after beating Carlos at the US Open!
Off the pitch, Real Madrid's projected wage bill for the 2026-27 season has reached a record 707.1 million euros according to 2Playbook analysis.
Seven hundred and seven million? That is wild!

That covers sports salaries and transfer-fee amortisation across the club. But total revenue is projected at 1.405 billion euros with a net profit of 14.2 million. Also, Iker Casillas has pulled his two sons, Martin and Lucas, out of La Fabrica.
Casillas really pulled both his kids out of the academy?

He did. Martin, who is twelve, lost his prominent role, and neither brother was selected for the Futures tournament in Orlando. So Casillas is moving both boys, who are goalkeepers, to Leganes. Lucas, who is ten, had saved several penalties against Barcelona during his two years at Madrid.
Footy Headlines also leaked Madrid's 125th anniversary kit for March 2027! Pure white, Adidas branding, a special gold patch, and the original intertwined M, C, F initials badge!
Over to cricket. India assistant coach Sitanshu Kotak spoke highly of KL Rahul ahead of the third ODI in Hamilton.
Kotak loves Rahul's flexibility, doesn't he?
He does. He pointed out Rahul can open in Tests, play middle order in ODIs, or hit out with five overs left. He highlighted his unbeaten 26 on that difficult Wellington pitch in the second ODI.
And Kane Williamson talked about Virat Kohli on a podcast!

Williamson revealed he called Kohli the day before announcing his retirement in June. He said it was like looking in a mirror, sharing parallel lives with captaincy and having children at the same time.
What about the IPL trade news? So Hardik is actually leaving Mumbai?
It is close. Hardik Pandya's trade from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings is nearing completion before the November 17 retention deadline. He will reunite with Punjab Kings head coach Ricky Ponting.

Novak Djokovic is out of the ATP Finals race, and Jim Courier questioned where he will end his career, suggesting the Los Angeles Olympics. Rafael Nadal told AP that Djokovic is not in the WhatsApp group chat he shares with Roger Federer because Novak is still competing.
Is Djokovic really aiming for the Los Angeles Olympics? That would be something.
In the NBA, Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard has a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his left thumb and will miss the game against New Orleans.
And Oscar Piastri has mutually split from his management team, Mark and Ann Webber, after four seasons in Formula One.
Back in Brazil, Lando Norris won after being jumped by Antonelli at the start, pitting on lap 16, and pressuring Antonelli into an error to take the lead.

spoken: Seriously Dhruv, you sit down early in Hamilton, toss happens, and then rain? Not a single ball bowled in the third ODI.
It is frustrating, Kylo, but look at the series. India lead 2-0 after three matches against New Zealand. Would you take 2-0 up with two to play?
I mean, yes, the series is in our control. But you want to watch cricket! Next up is the fourth ODI at Mount Maunganui on Friday morning.

Before that, New Zealand named a 14-member squad for their two-Test series against India. Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, and Tom Blundell are all in, even while recovering from injuries. Conway had a concussion in training before this ODI series, Ravindra hurt his shoulder during a photoshoot in September, and Blundell has a quad issue. Head coach Rob Walter says he is looking forward to hosting India.
Good to see them back soon. Over in football, did you see what Vinícius Junior did?
I did. A lovely gesture.

He sent a personal video message in Arabic to Zaher, a 13-year-old boy in Cairo who lost both his legs in a drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan. Zaher got prosthetic legs after a BBC report, and Vini popped up on screen saying Zaher, mahaba. What a heart on that guy.

Class from Vini. On the pitch, though, Kylian Mbappé has a hamstring issue. He missed France's final team session before traveling to Milan for their match against Italy, and he is receiving treatment under medical supervision.
Zidane will not want to risk him at all, nor will Madrid. Speaking of Madrid managers, Thibaut Courtois gave an interview talking about Jose Mourinho coming back to replace Alvaro Arbeloa.
Did Courtois really leave Jose on read for two weeks?

He did! Courtois said Mourinho texted him when he took the job, but Courtois was on a flight during the World Cup with no Wi-Fi. Ignored it for two weeks by mistake! He asked someone at Madrid if it was really the coach's number before replying. But he said he is very happy to work with Mourinho again after their Chelsea days.
Classic Courtois. Right, IPL news now.
Massive news! The trade is official. Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings completed a swap. Hardik Pandya goes to Punjab, and Arshdeep Singh moves to Mumbai.

Hardik is 33, gives Punjab an all-rounder across three departments after a tough second stint with MI. Mumbai get a frontline fast bowler for their powerplay and death overs. Neither team made playoffs last season, so both are reshaping.
Huge move for both sides! And speaking of Indian cricket, Aaryavir Sehwag just smashed 160 for India U19 against UAE!

160 with 17 fours and seven sixes. India hit 309 for seven, then Ishan Sood took four for 37 to bowl UAE out for 239. A 70-run win puts India into Thursday's U19 Asia Cup semi-final against Afghanistan.
That name on the back of the jersey hitting sixes, love to see it. Also in Indian cricket news, remember Lee Fortis? The Surrey curator who argued with Gautam Gambhir at The Oval in 2025?
Why did Lee Fortis leave Surrey then?

He left the club after disciplinary proceedings following another row during The Hundred in July. Sitanshu Kotak recalled how Fortis shouted at Indian staff to stay two and a half metres away from the pitch, and Gambhir told him, You are just a groundsman and nothing beyond.

Firm words. On Suryakumar Yadav, he spoke about his current situation. After leading India to the T20 World Cup title earlier this year, he acknowledged it has been a very difficult phase being out of the national team reckoning.
He will bounce back, no doubt. Right, Max Verstappen!
Max came from P21 to finish second in São Paulo behind Lando Norris, but he wants answers from Red Bull.
He drove brilliantly on the intermediate tyres in the wet, but once he switched to soft tyres, he had extreme oversteer. Max said the car felt wrong and Red Bull must investigate what happened.
Fair call when you are pushing for wins. In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev are the first two players confirmed for Team Europe at the 2027 Laver Cup in Los Angeles at the Intuit Dome.

And Juan Carlos Ferrero gave an interview to Marca about Alcaraz. Ferrero, who won Roland Garros in 2003 and was world number one, coached Carlos for seven years until late 2025. He will coach Ben Shelton from 2027, but he said Alcaraz is one hundred percent favourite for the ATP Finals and Davis Cup, and hopes they reunite naturally in Turin.
Also, Lorenzo Musetti said Zverev deserves his year-end number one spot, but added that a healthy Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner are a class above.
Over to the NBA, Golden State Warriors just demolished the New Orleans Pelicans 138 to 87!

An eight-game winning streak now. Steph Curry tore them apart early. Golden State are 8-3 and went unbeaten on their five-game homestand. Though backup guard Brandon Williams left after 99 seconds with a mild left hamstring strain.

Yeah, his MRI confirmed he is out for at least a week. That adds to Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody, Gary Payton II, Will Richard with a torn thumb ligament, and Kristaps Porzingis who is practically retired.
It was also Jordan Poole's return to Golden State. He was drafted 28th in 2019, won the 2022 title, but after the Draymond Green punch, he was traded. A 51-point beating for his Pelicans tonight.
In tennis, Novak Djokovic has partnered with Aman Group to launch ATMA, an ultra-luxury wellness brand. Their first spot is ATMA Miami in Brickell, a 1,049-foot tower designed by SHoP Architects.
And Jannik Sinner says he aims to return at the Australian Open in January after his knee injury, working without rushing. He also split with his coach Darren Cahill after four years.
In Formula 1, F2 contender Nikola Tsolov gets a test with Racing Bulls at the Hungaroring in an older Honda car this week. Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are still waiting on seat announcements.

Also, F1 confirmed the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix will go ahead as planned. No extra engine upgrades were granted under the FIA upgrade scheme, and Esteban Ocon broke his silence following his Haas exit.

Around the grounds, renowned sport and music broadcaster Danny Kelly has died at 69 from throat cancer. The former NME editor and long-time talkSPORT host was a massive Tottenham fan, and tributes have poured in from across football.

Why Racing Bulls stuck with Lawson and Lindblad
Why did Pierre Sage resign from Crystal Palace without being 'officially' sacked?
spoken: Let me start with Real Madrid. Our one-hundred-and-twenty-five-million-euro winger Yan Diomande was filmed handing out money to young supporters while on international duty with Ivory Coast before their Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Gambia.

A lovely gesture ahead of Herve Renard's squad preparations. And speaking of Madrid, the Royal Spanish Football Federation has formally submitted a bid to host the 2027 UEFA Nations League Final Four. If successful, the Santiago Bernabeu is set to host the final alongside Valladolid's Jose Zorrilla Stadium.
Imagine hosting that final at the Bernabeu! What about Michael Olise though? Are we still tracking him?

Reports from L'Equipe say Real Madrid's interest has not faded, even after Bayern Munich turned down an offer over five hundred million euros last summer. Bayern want to extend his deal past 2029, but his French international teammates Mbappe, Konate and Camavinga keep reminding him how special the Bernabeu is.
They know what they are talking about! Now, what is the word from the Indian camp in New Zealand?

New Zealand have called up pacer Brett Randell for the fourth and fifth ODIs following his County Championship run with Derbyshire. All-rounder Josh Clarkson joins for the fifth ODI, and head coach Rob Walter indicated Randell is likely to make his debut.
And Rishabh Pant is officially back!
He passed his fitness test at the Centre of Excellence after his side strain and shared a picture from his flight to New Zealand. He will be ready for the first Test starting Wednesday.
And that massive IPL trade deal between Punjab Kings and Mumbai Indians?
Punjab Kings co-owner Ness Wadia confirmed trading Arshdeep Singh was tough, but he believes acquiring Hardik Pandya gives the Shreyas Iyer-led team the championship touch they have been missing.
Over in Formula One, Lando Norris dominated Brazil, but managed to shatter his champagne bottle on the podium!

He certainly did. Meanwhile, Ralf Schumacher noted on Sky Sports Germany that Max Verstappen would find moving to Mercedes difficult because he is so technical, having grown up with his father Jos. You said last show, "He will bounce back, no doubt. Right, Max Verstappen!" He did storm to second from twenty-first, but Ralf thinks a team switch would be complicated.
Max adapts to anything! What about Carlos Alcaraz in Turin?

In the ATP Finals draw, Alcaraz lands in a group with Frances Tiafoe, Flavio Cobolli and Daniil Medvedev. Alexander Zverev faces a tougher path with Rafael Jodar, Ben Shelton and Arthur Fils. Alcaraz was seen practicing with a bandage on his right knee, but reports confirm it is purely precautionary.

Back to the NBA. Golden State fell one-hundred-and-fifteen to one-hundred-and-eight at Houston, breaking the eight-game streak. Alperen Sengun almost had a triple-double with nineteen points, thirteen rebounds and nine assists, while Kevin Durant scored twenty.

The bigger concern is Steph Curry. He strained his right abdominal area after tangling with Sengun in the first quarter, sank a three-pointer, grabbed his side, and went straight for an MRI. Steve Kerr admitted concern is high.
And Marcus Smart got thrown out for punching Charles Bassey late in the third quarter!

Smart got his arm tangled with Bassey and threw a blow to the head area. Elsewhere in tennis, Rinky Hijikata beat Novak Djokovic six-two, three-six, three-six in Paris, climbing to a career-high ranking of fifty-nine.
Any other motorsport news?

George Russell launched the GR63 Academy, offering young drivers qualifier trials at Silverstone. And Racing Bulls confirmed their driver pairing for next season, keeping Liam Lawson and rookie Arvid Lindblad.

Around the grounds, Pierre Sage has stepped down as Crystal Palace manager. By stepping aside rather than being officially sacked, Palace avoid paying financial compensation while Lens avoid a transfer fee.
